raw_segments.text: Having crossed the marsh, I saw a trace of white over the moor. I approached it. It was
a road or a track. It led straight up to the light, which now beamed from a sort of knoll
amidst a clump of trees—furs, apparently, from what I could distinguish of the character
of their forms and foliage through the gloom. My star vanished as I drew near. Some obstacle
had intervened between me and it.
I put out my hand to feel the dark mass before me. I discriminated the rough stones of a
low wall above it, something like palisades and within a high and prickly hedge. I groped
on. Again, a whitish object gleamed before me. It was a gate. A wicket. It moved on
its hinges as I touched it. On each side stood a sable bush, holly or you.
